why_this_matters: Day 75 sits in Phase 5 (Data Visualization + Storytelling), whose goal is: Turn data into charts that change decisions, in matplotlib, seaborn and plotly. Today's core material - Five-number summary visualised, IQR fences on the plot, Violin plots and density shapes - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

code.code:
# Import library
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

# Sample data
data = [[2, 2], [3, 3], [3, 4], [30, 30], [31, 31], [32, 32]]

# Create a K-means model with two clusters (normal and outlier)
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=2, n_init=10)
kmeans.fit(data)

# Predict cluster labels
labels = kmeans.predict(data)

# Identify outliers based on cluster labels
outliers = [data[i] for i, label in enumerate(labels) if label == 1]

# print data
print("Data:", data)
print("Outliers:", outliers)
# Remove outliers
data = [data[i] for i, label in enumerate(labels) if label == 0]
print("Data without outliers:", data)

# Step 6: Print the outliers
print(f"Here are the outliers based on the z-score threshold, 3:\n {data[data['Z-Score'] > 3]}")
print("----------------------------------------")

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Five-number summary visualised on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
